required_stages.description: Allocate a fresh (n,) output of x's dtype inside run().
One kernel pass that reads each element of x once, replaces negatives by zero (select or max), and stores once at the same position, with correct tail handling for n elements.

forbidden_substitutions.message: The clamp must be performed by the kernel, not by a PyTorch op.
Tensor-method clamp/relu/maximum or a host copy inside run() replaces the whole computation.
Returning the input, a view of it, or a host-side expression on it replaces the whole computation.
No dtype conversion is allowed anywhere in relu.
No initialised scratch or host-side copy is part of this operator (an in-kernel zero tile is fine; a torch zero tensor is not needed).

required_evidence.message: No kernel-level store found; the map must be done by a kernel.
No compare/select or maximum against zero found inside the kernel.

outputs.aliasing: none; the returned (n,) tensor must be freshly allocated inside run() and must not share storage with x

timing_boundary.notes: Everything inside run() is timed: the output allocation and the single elementwise kernel. No cached state, no host-side copy or conversion of x.
